added_models.model: Dutch Belted rabbit, invasive episcleral venous pressure, topical netarsudil 0.04%

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Filed with the NDA as study AR-13324-APH08 (FDA PharmR 2017).
engagement.note: Netarsudil 0.04% cut episcleral venous pressure 35% and IOP 39% in Dutch Belted rabbits, measured by servonull micropipette.
engagement.quote: Three hours after AR-13324 dosing, IOP was reduced by 39%±7% (P<0.001) and EVP decreased by 35%±4% (P<0.05); after vehicle dosing, IOP was reduced by 24%±4% (P<0.05) and EVP increased by 25%±5% (P<0.05).
engagement.judgement: Opens at the paper's online date (2015-03); the human aqueous-dynamics study NCT02406287 started 2015-04, so the prediction was prospective.

engagement.magnitude_basis: % fall in episcleral venous pressure (rabbit 0.04% day 3 vs human 0.02% day 8)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Kazemi: 'Diurnal EVP was not significantly different between netarsudil- and placebo-treated eyes.' Sit 2021 (doi 10.1016/j.ajo.2021.01.019; NCT03233308, results 2019-06-11) found a significant -0.89 mmHg treatment difference in POAG/OHT patients; changes no status. FDA ClinPharmR (2017-08-28) states EVP reduction was shown 'in animal and human studies'.
engagement.note: EVP fell 10% in netarsudil-treated healthy-volunteer eyes versus 35% in rabbits; not significant against the vehicle eye.
engagement.quote: Diurnal episcleral venous pressure (EVP) in netarsudil-treated eyes decreased from 7.9 ± 1.2 mmHg to 7.2 ± 1.8 (-10%; P = 0.01).
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Kazemi does not cite the rabbit data in the abstract. Within-eye fall significant, between-eye difference not, hence partial. 35% vs 10% is 3.5-fold.

added_models.model: Perfused enucleated human donor eyes, netarsudil-M1 0.3 μM

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Filed with the NDA as study AR-13324-IPH05 (FDA PharmR 2017); FDA ClinPharmR cites 'perfused human eyes' as mechanism evidence.
engagement.note: Netarsudil's active metabolite raised outflow facility 51% over baseline in perfused human donor eyes and dilated episcleral veins.
engagement.quote: Perfusion with netarsudil-M1 significantly increased C when compared to baseline (51%, P < 0.01) and to paired controls (102%, P < 0.01), as well as significantly increased PEFL in both IW (P < 0.05) and ESVs (P < 0.01).
engagement.judgement: Human tissue but not a dosed person, so a model (ex_vivo). Published 2016-11, before human outflow-facility data were public (NCT02406287 completed 2016-04, no posted results, published 2018), so prospective as far as public record shows.

engagement.magnitude_basis: % increase in outflow facility over baseline (ex-vivo 3 h perfusion vs human tonography day 8)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Sit 2021 (POAG/OHT patients) repeated the rise; Kim 2024 (doi 10.1016/j.xops.2024.100533) found episcleral vessel diameter up ~27% in patients, matching the ex-vivo ESV dilation. Neither changes the status.
engagement.note: Outflow facility rose 22% in dosed healthy volunteers versus 51% in perfused donor eyes; same direction, smaller.
engagement.quote: In netarsudil-treated eyes, diurnal outflow facility increased from 0.27 ± 0.10 μL/min/mmHg to 0.33 ± 0.11 μL/min/mmHg (+22%; P = 0.02) after 7 days of treatment.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me. Ex-vivo dosing was the active metabolite at a fixed perfusate concentration, so the dose link is loose; 51% vs 22% is 2.3-fold. Kept to engagement: the system made no IOP or dose prediction for patients.

added_models.model: Living mouse eye, OCT of conventional outflow tissue, topical netarsudil

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); facility magnitude not in abstract. Not among the NDA pharmacology studies.
engagement.note: Topical netarsudil widened trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal on OCT, raised outflow facility and lowered IOP in living mice.
engagement.quote: These changes occurred in conjunction with increased outflow facility, increased speckle variance intensity of outflow vessels, increased tracer deposition in conventional outflow tissues and decreased intraocular pressure.
engagement.judgement: Opens at the online date (2016-04). Sponsor co-authored mechanism study, run after the Phase 3 IOP results but before human outflow data, so not a retrodiction for engagement.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both sides; mouse facility magnitude unknown, so direction only.
engagement.note: Outflow facility rose 22% in dosed healthy volunteers, the direction the mouse showed; no human OCT of Schlemm's canal was found.
engagement.quote: In netarsudil-treated eyes, diurnal outflow facility increased from 0.27 ± 0.10 μL/min/mmHg to 0.33 ± 0.11 μL/min/mmHg (+22%; P = 0.02) after 7 days of treatment.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me. Only the facility readout has a human counterpart; the OCT canal readouts were never measured in dosed patients that I found.

added_models.model: ARHGEF12 rs11824032 risk genotype (African-ancestry POAG GWAS) as predictor of netarsudil response

efficacy.confidence_note: Opening date from the cited GWAS (Verma 2024, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2023.12.006, PMID 38242088, taken from the reference list; not read).
efficacy.note: African-ancestry GWAS (Verma 2024, Cell) mapped a POAG risk allele to ARHGEF12, a RhoA activator upstream of ROCK.
efficacy.quote: Variants within the Rho/ROCK signaling pathway, including loci at ARHGEF12 and ROCK1P1, were identified based on prior genome-wide association analyses
efficacy.judgement: Opens at the GWAS year, when the genotype became available as a candidate patient selector for ROCK inhibitors.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: difference in ≥20% IOP-reduction rate by genotype
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text (PMC13194400). Retrospective EHR cohort, n=66 (114 eyes), most on concurrent medications; aOR 1.31 (95% CI 0.42-4.10). The hypothesis was undirected ('may influence response').
efficacy.note: In 66 netarsudil-treated POAG patients, ARHGEF12 carriers and non-carriers reached ≥20% IOP reduction at similar rates (35% vs 30%).
efficacy.quote: ARHGEF12 variant carriers did not show a statistically significant difference in treatment response assessed by IOP; however, given the small sample size, particularly among homozygous carriers, and concurrent use of multiple glaucoma medications, these findings should be interpreted cautiously
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: the paper tests the genotype's prediction against patient IOP response. Scored contra because the source says the genotype 'does not strongly predict' response; low confidence because the null is underpowered and exploratory. Netarsudil was already approved, but the patient-level answer was not known, so not a retrodiction.

added_models.model: New Zealand white rabbit, normotensive and acute hypertensive IOP plus hyperemia scoring, topical AMA0076 (sovesudil)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Opening year is a proxy: the rabbit work preceded the first-in-human study NCT01693315 (start 2012-09); paper online 2014-02-18.
efficacy.note: AMA0076 (sovesudil) lowered IOP in normotensive and acutely hypertensive New Zealand white rabbits, as well as Y-39983 did.
efficacy.quote: Administration of AMA0076 effectively reduces IOP in ocular normotensive and acute hypertensive rabbits without causing distinct hyperemia.
efficacy.judgement: Sovesudil's own model, distinct from the netarsudil monkey/rabbit track. Opens at the first-in-human start year as proxy for first use.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of IOP change from baseline
efficacy.confidence_note: Tier 5 sponsor release (2013-11-14); NCT01693315 has no posted results and no paper. Ha 2021 (tier 1, normal-tension glaucoma) repeated the IOP fall; listed in patient_trials, changes no status. NCT02136940 (Phase 2, POAG) has no posted results.
efficacy.reason: IOP fell in patients as predicted

patient_trials.quote: 0.5% sovesudil TID met the criteria for superiority to the placebo.

efficacy.note: In the first-in-human trial the best AMA0076 dose cut mean diurnal IOP 3.7 mmHg from baseline (p=0.020 vs placebo), as the rabbits predicted.
efficacy.quote: The results seen so far with AMA0076 suggest that the promise seen in pre-clinical development has been carried into the clinic successfully.
efficacy.judgement: Stated by an investigator in the sponsor release. Year 2014: the release (2013-11) predates the rabbit paper (2014-02), so the comparison was public only once both sides were. Rabbit work preceded the trial, so not retro.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Opening year is a proxy: the rabbit work preceded the first-in-human study NCT01693315 (start 2012-09); paper online 2014-02-18.
safety.note: Single topical AMA0076 gave significantly less conjunctival hyperemia than Y-39983 in rabbits, the design goal of a locally acting ROCK inhibitor.
safety.quote: The degree of hyperemia was significantly lower in rabbits treated with AMA0076 then with Y-39983.
safety.judgement: Named harm with a stated prediction (little hyperemia) checkable in patients.

safety.confidence_note: Tier 5 sponsor release; no posted results for NCT01693315. Ha 2021 (doi 10.1111/aos.14949, NTG, TID dosing) later reported hyperaemia in 24.4% (0.5%) and 17.5% (0.25%), mostly mild, which the authors call 'relatively low'; changes no status.
safety.reason: Little hyperemia in patients, as predicted
safety.note: No hyperemia-related adverse events at the most effective dose in the first-in-human trial; rabbits had predicted minimal hyperemia.
safety.quote: To see such low levels of hyperemia accompanying meaningful reductions in IOP is a breakthrough in the development of ROCK inhibitors.
safety.judgement: Same release; the investigator ties the clinical hyperemia result to the preclinical promise. Year 2014 as for efficacy.

considered_not_added: ATS907 normotensive cynomolgus monkey IOP (Hsu & Kengatharan, ARVO 2011): model side is a conference abstract with no DOI/PMID, and the Phase 2 failure (NCT01520116, NCT01668524, no results) is known only from a review; no admissible patient source.
DE-104 (Santen): no public model data found; Phase 2 trials NCT00650338/NCT00657579/NCT00656240/NCT00868894 have no posted results.
Dutch Belted rabbit IOP lowering (Wang 2015, Lin 2017): same normotensive-animal IOP system the draft's main strip already tracks.
Rocklatan (netarsudil/latanoprost, NDA 208259) animal combination data: PharmR 208259 holds no separate pharmacology model; any additivity data are the same normotensive-animal system.
Human trabecular meshwork / Schlemm's canal cell cultures (actin stress fibres, focal adhesions, fibrosis markers): readouts never measured in dosed patients; no patient comparison.

Corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertensive mouse treated with netarsudil (Li 2019 PNAS, Li 2021 eLife): no member-drug trial in steroid-induced glaucoma to compare with; outside the unselected OAG population.
Corneal verticillata: no predictive model beyond the monkey ocular toxicology the draft already tracks in safety.
In-silico / QSP dose models, patient-derived cells, human challenge models: none found for netarsudil, ATS907 or DE-104.
Ripasudil (Japan) models and trials: ripasudil is not a member drug of this tile.
Verosudil (AR-12286) monkey outflow/IOP (Wang RF, ARVO 2009 e-abstract 1465): conference abstract with no DOI/PMID, so no admissible model side.
Verosudil (AR-12286) steroid-induced OHT mouse (Ren 2023, doi 10.1167/iovs.64.2.7): run after patient IOP results (2011) and in steroid-induced OHT, with no AR-12286 trial in that population.
RKI983 (Novartis): no publication; NCT00846989 and NCT00515424 have no posted results; no model data found.

gaps.detail: Model side is an ARVO abstract with no DOI/PMID (rule 2 tier 1); Phase 2 NCT01668524 (completed) and NCT01520116 (unknown) have no posted results, failure known only from a review.
No public DE-104 model data; NCT00650338/NCT00657579/NCT00656240/NCT00868894 have no posted results; discontinuation only in a review (not a source, rule 2).
Not a member drug of this tile (members: ATS907, DE-104, RKI983, netarsudil, sovesudil, verosudil).

AR-12286 is verosudil; its monkey data are only ARVO 2009 e-abstracts (no DOI/PMID, rule 2); Williams 2011 patient trial has no tier 1-3 model to pair with; Ren 2023 SIOH mouse is retro and off-population.
Europe PMC: no papers; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00846989, NCT00515424 completed with no results; no model data found.
nzw-rabbit-iop-sovesudil: efficacy and safety (hyperemia) untested 2012 -> same 2014 (Van de Velde 2014 rabbit vs Amakem 2013 FIH release; Ha 2021 NTG Phase II as patient_trial).
Same as AR-12286: no peer-reviewed or regulator model data before its patient trials (Williams 2011, Kopczynski 2013, Skaat 2016); only ARVO abstracts and a 2023 retro steroid mouse.
